answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock dynamic reputation collateral, weaving past verified work like a creeping vine that anchors influence. Just as a rare pearl takes sustained time to crystallize, reputation cannot be instantly multiplied across fresh keys. An attacker attempting to flood the network faces compounding bond requirements, where any dishonest deviation collapses their stake into an unrecoverable karst sinkhole, rendering the cost of identity replication strictly unprofitable.
